newsitem.title: MEXICO: UN agency sees Mexico economy decelerating in Q1.
newsitem.headline: UN agency sees Mexico economy decelerating in Q1.

text.p: Mexico's economy showed some signs of deceleration in the 1997 first quarter from the dynamism that was seen last year, the United Nations Economic Commision for Latin America (CEPAL) said Monday in a report.
The commission also said there were major differences in the behavior of different sectors of the economy.
"Exports and investment continue to be the dynamic elements of demand, while the recovery of consumption is being delayed," CEPAL said in a news release.

CEPAL said private consumption had lost four percentage points of its share of Mexican gross domestic product between 1994 and 1996, "which shows the difficulties in improving the wellbeing of the majority of the population."
Signs of deceleration had been observed in industrial production, car sales and the import of intermediate goods, it said.

CEPAL said it predicted GDP growth of 4.5 percent this year, inflation of 18 percent, an exchange rate of 8.50 to 9.0 pesos to the dollar by December, and a public sector deficit of slightly more than one percent of GDP.

The commission also predicted continued slow growth in private consumption and a tendency for export growth to slow. It said Mexico's trade surplus was likely to shrink as imports grew, leading to a trade deficit in the second half of 1997. The year overall is likely to produce a trade surplus but the current account balance of payments will go further into the red because of interest payments on foreign debt, it said.
